draft.title: Divided Berlin
card: After 1945, Germany was divided into four zones run by the USA, Britain, France and the Soviet Union. Berlin lay inside the Soviet zone and was also split into four sectors.
The three western sectors became West Berlin, linked to West Germany. The Soviet sector became East Berlin, in communist East Germany.
Many East Germans left through West Berlin to live in the West. In 1961, East Germany built the Berlin Wall to stop them.
The Wall stood until 1989, when it fell. It became a symbol of the division between East and West.
draft.remember: Berlin was split after 1945, and the Wall of 1961 to 1989 stopped East Germans leaving.

a.q: Why did East Germany build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
opts: To stop East Germans leaving for the West
To keep West Germans out of East Berlin
To mark the border between Germany and Poland
To protect East Berlin from a Western invasion
a.why: Many East Germans were leaving through West Berlin, so the Wall was built to stop them. The Wall was aimed at keeping people in, not at keeping invaders out.
a.clue: Think about which way people were moving.

b.q: Lena lived in East Berlin in 1970. Which description fits her situation?
opts: She could not freely cross into West Berlin
She lived in a sector run by the USA
She could cross to West Berlin whenever she liked
She lived in a city that was not divided
b.why: The Wall stood from 1961 to 1989, so East Berliners could not freely cross it. East Berlin was the Soviet sector, not a US one.
b.clue: Check whether the Wall stood in 1970.

a.best: To stop East Germans leaving for the West

b.best: She could not freely cross into West Berlin
